title: Heterogeneous-bandwidth-aware batch steering and attention-kernel hedging for multi-GPU schedules
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In heterogeneous GPU racks (mixed NVLink/NVSwitch islands and PCIe-only nodes) we observe suboptimal overlap between all-reduce communications and compute during prefill/decode, and frequent fallback to slower attention kernels for uncommon sequence/window sizes. This leads to higher tail-latency and lower effective throughput for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters.

Goal: Implement a runtime steering layer that (1) measures per-request and per-topology bandwidth/latency signals at runtime, (2) dynamically steers micro-batches to devices and comm-windows to maximize NCCL overlap, and (3) hedges kernel selection by preferring fused/tiling attention kernels when predicted to benefit latency or reduce comm pressure. The feature should be safe (no regression in correctness), observable, and toggleable per-customer.

Scope: This ticket covers design, prototype implementation in the conductor, benchmark harness commits, and a canary rollout on a dedicated heterogeneous test cluster. Not in scope: hardware changes, large-scale account rollout (separate rollout ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can classify node interconnect topology (NVLink island, NVSwitch, PCIe-only) at boot and expose a lightweight bandwidth metric per device.
Scheduler can detect low-utilization comm windows and opportunistically schedule all-reduce ops to overlap with decode for at least 3 workload profiles.

Kernel-selection hedging is implemented: for attention windows where fused-kernel latency prediction < fallback kernel latency by >=5%, the runtime prefers fused kernels; otherwise it falls back. No correctness regressions across model suite.

Benchmarks on heterogeneous testbed (Llama-2-13B, seq=1024, batch shapes used in customer workloads) show >=10% throughput uplift or >=15% 95th-percentile latency reduction vs baseline scheduling in at least two of three profiles.
Feature has observability: per-request routing logs, model-level telemetry of hedging decisions, and dashboard with comm-overlap ratio and kernel-choice distribution.
Canary rollout on dedicated test cluster completed with no reliability regressions for 48 hours and approval from SRE/Perf guild.
tasks: Design: define topology detection signals and lightweight bandwidth estimator (Aisha + Diego)
Prototype: implement bandwidth probe and comm-window detector in conductor (Diego)
Kernel predictor: train a small latency predictor for attention kernels based on seq_len, batch, device-type (Riya)
Scheduler integration: implement micro-batch steering policy and hedging hooks (Diego + Marco)
Benchmarks: add harness scenarios (LLama-2-13B, gpt-like profiles) and run baseline vs steering (Perf team)
Observability: add structured logs, traces, and Grafana panels for comm-overlap and kernel decisions (SRE + Observability)
PRs: open split PRs for conductor changes, kernel predictor, and scheduler policy; include unit/integration tests
Canary: deploy to hetero-test cluster, run smoke + perf tests, collect 48h metrics and rollback plan

2026-03-11 - Diego Morales: Proto bandwidth probe implemented in conductor branch 'bandwidth-probe'. Early microbenchmarks show clear distinctions between NVSwitch and PCIe nodes (bandwidth ratio ~8x on our test rack).

2026-03-11 - Riya Sen: Started kernel-latency predictor dataset collection. Ran Llama-2-13B attention microbenchmarks across fused vs fallback kernels for window sizes {32,64,128,256} and devices (A100-80GB, H100-80GB). Results show fused wins for small windows <64 in many cases when comm overlaps are present.
